Test-suite performance work remains complete: customer, subscription, report, invoice, and payment tests were optimized using batched/shared fixtures and persisted factories. Invoice tests pass (46), payment tests pass (63), and the full suite previously passed in 14.92s with 318 passed, 4 skipped, and no warnings. Production billing behavior was not changed.

The intermittent invoice-sync 409 was investigated and fixed. Repeated concurrent POSTs with the same idempotency key reproduced the issue, and the database showed the key stuck in `processing` after a successful request. `InvoiceSyncService.submit` was confirmed not to persist completion itself. The repository claim update was made conditional on both the key and invoice ID, preventing an incorrect completion/replay race. All 8 integration tests now pass, including the duplicate-sync case; 14 invoice-sync unit tests also pass. A regression test now verifies that concurrent duplicate syncs return the original invoice response. A 200-request stress test produced 8 submissions and 192 replays, no 500s, exactly one persisted key, and a completed response matching the original request.

Remaining work: resolve `test_apply_credit_after_refund` (expected 87.50 versus 90.00, likely credit/refund ordering); complete and validate `split-order-rules-package`; fix the trial-balance fixture/query issue; verify rebuild entry points and tenant migration helpers use the optimized shared search path; and review remaining ledger entry points and unannotated billing functions. Continue observing replica host, Bandit, Cloud Run cost, CI/runtime approval, and `invoice_renderer_v26` requirements.

Validation is complete: the integration suite passes 8/8, unit tests pass 14/14, and a new concurrent duplicate-sync regression test verifies both requests resolve to `INV-1042`. The database contains one completed `load-42` idempotency row whose stored response matches the first successful request.
